digest.component_or_area: rebar graph link store and reconciler
propositions: Write operations are relation-scoped (idempotent per target_id and relation) allowing one pair to hold multiple relations, but removal is pair-scoped and returns only the most recent link without a relation parameter, causing asymmetry

When a pair holds two relations (e.g. blocks and relates_to) and a peer deletes one relation, the inbound reconciler permanently declines to remove the other due to relation mismatch in guard G5, causing non-convergence

The outbound differ dedupes direction-agnostically on vendor type without considering relation, allowing a same-vendor-type remote link to suppress outbound re-add and let inbound removal records survive unchallenged to guard G5
Relation-scoped removal seam in graph/_links.py::remove_dependency mirrors add_dependency by keying removal on (target_id, relation) and validates the exact relation before writing UNLINK events
Reconciler inbound path (_inbound_unlink_one) must use relation-scoped removal instead of pair-scoped unlink to converge when double-related pairs experience peer deletion of one relation
CLI rebar unlink gains optional relation argument for relation-scoped behavior while preserving backward-compatible pair-scoped most-recent removal when no relation is supplied
